newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas loses more ground on temps.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas loses more ground on temps.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures continued to lose ground late Wednesday in moderate activity, still pressured by bearish weather forecasts and some technical selling, industry sources said.
At 1405 EST, April skidded 9.8 cents to $1.845 per million British thermal units, while May was 6.9 cents lower at $1.91. Other months were down by one to 5.2 cents.

"I don't think the AGA number will mean anything. We know the weather through March 15, so I don't think prices are going anywhere. We'll probably just stay in a range," said one Houston trader, noting plenty of mild weather ahead.
He said he did not expect spot futures to break out of the recent range between $1.70 and $2.00.
But some expected typically-weak spring demand and bloated eastern storage to lead to more downside.

"I don't think we've seen the bottom yet. The eastern LDCs (utilities) don't have to buy any gas. They're going to be in the driver's seat at least through April and will try to force prices lower," said one East Coast trader.
Withdrawal estimates for today's American Gas Association storage report range from 40 to 105 bcf, with most expecting a draw in the 70-80 bcf range. Last year, stocks fell by 62 bcf.
Technically, traders said recent ranges were intact, with April support still at $1.78-1.80, then in the mid-$1.70s and the contract low of $1.701. Resistance was seen at $1.965 and then $2.04.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices gained about five cents Wednesday to about the $1.90 level. Midcon pipes were up a dime to the low-$1.80s. New York city gate swing gas firmed about 10 cents to the $2.20 area.
NYMEX said 27,453 Hub contracts traded as of 1330 EST. Hub open interest on March 4 rose 5,359 contracts to 167,668.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1400 EST.

On the KCBT, April slipped five cents to $1.66, while deferreds were down up one-half to six cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 4.8 cents to 18.5 cents (NYMEX premium). ((J Silha, New York Power Desk 212-859-1624))
